relation_to_prior_protocols.mover-v3-draft-20260924: The archived full draft. This core carries over its H1 and H3 definitions, restricted as item_set states, and the rules it names. The core governs wherever the two differ.

question: Among US-equity extreme daily movers (population D), does MAX lottery conditioning (H1), or the overnight versus intraday split of the hold (H3), change the sign or size of the cost-net forward return? Continuation is one tested outcome, not the premise.
direction: long only (a short side for the MAX-reversal prior is an open question; borrow, hard-to-borrow fees and SEC Rule 201 were not examined)

item_set.family: m = 5: two primary tests that are not tradable (H1-D, H3-c) and three tradable cells (H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b). Holm runs over these five items only.

items.statistic: mean net(b_lane | high MAX21 tercile) - mean net(b_lane | low MAX21 tercile), population D
items.why_kept: The direct test of H1. BCW 2011 predicts that high-MAX names underperform low-MAX names. The high-minus-low difference on one arm is the smallest statistic that tests that prediction. The 5-session b_lane arm is kept because it is the D horizon closest to BCW's holding period.

items.statistic: mean net(b_lane | low MAX21 tercile), population D
items.why_kept: The study is long-only and asks about cost-net returns. The low-MAX tercile is the only H1 cell for which the prior predicts the best relative return, so it is the one cell whose pass would make the conditioning tradable. The high and middle cells (high has a negative prior, middle none) are reported descriptively with no p-value.

The intraday leg as a trade: one regular session, from 09:35 to 15:55 ET on t+1. With H3-b it answers whether either leg is tradable after costs. Neither leg has a sourced direction for movers, so both are kept.
The overnight leg as a trade: from 15:55 ET on t+1 to the first eligible quote from 09:30 ET on t+2. It is the counterpart of H3-a.

items.statistic: mean over events of (mean of the 4 overnight leg log returns - mean of the 4 intraday leg log returns), gross, legs as in arms.c_decomposition
items.alternative: not equal to 0 at development; after development, one-sided in the direction of the development estimate (multiple_testing.direction_lock)
items.why_kept: The direct test of H3's 'versus'. It uses official prints only, so it needs no fill and no cost model. The literature (LPS 2019, ABJK 2022) concerns large, liquid names and gives no sign for movers, so the test is two-sided until development locks the direction.

item_set.tradable_cells: H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a and H3-b are tradable cells and nothing else. H1-D and H3-c are primary tests and are never tradable cells. The robustness requirement (statistics.robustness_required_for_a_pass) applies to the three tradable cells only.
item_set.dropped_from_the_full_draft: Population I and its minute-trigger formulas: it is a second population with its own open finding (the listing-exchange opening print can come after decision minute m), and neither H1 nor H3 needs it. The H1 arms a_fast and c_session and their 12 cells (6 per population): they multiplied cells without adding a test of the conditioning. H1-I and the 9 I-lane cells. The holdout cap of 5 tradable cells: with three tradable cells it has no work to do, so the gate opens for every validated item. The 2017-2019 cost re-measure: it is replaced by the per-fill realized half-spread floor (cost_model.per_side), which removes a pre-outcome stage whose quote stamps were outcome prices. H2, H4 and H5 (and their data gates) and H6: deferred (README appendix).

Development (2017-2019) and validation (2020) are therefore screening stages only. Validation decides which items the holdout gate opens for, but a validation pass is labelled 'screened', never confirmatory. Only the prospective holdout can support a confirmatory claim. Beside each validation result, the same statistic is reported on the least-exposed slice: symbol-sessions that were not a broad-universe lane decision (med20 of raw close x volume < $2M, fewer than 60 prior contiguous bars, or has_gap, as broad-universe protocol.json defines them). exposure_registry.update_rule: Every later read of data in any v3 window before the freeze is appended here with its date and purpose. No quote at a v3 entry, exit or terminal-search stamp is fetched before the freeze. Daily bars and official prints are fetched before the freeze only into the sealed pre_freeze_access_path snapshot, and are opened only by the count-only code. Any other pre-freeze read is forbidden, not tolerated. If one happens anyway, it is appended here and recorded as a numbered deviation before the freeze, and it voids development screening: no item can be nominated at development, so every item scores p = 1 in the validation Holm run. A read of a v3-defined outcome in the validation window before the freeze voids validation. A read in the holdout window before the gate opens voids the holdout.

pre_freeze_access_path.rule: Before the freeze, data are fetched only by committed count-only code in the study tree (run_discipline.study_code). Raw pages go straight into a private snapshot sealed by sha256. They are never opened by a person or by any other code. The count-only code emits only counts and rates: no price, spread, return, gain, covariate value, event list or symbol-level row. Its committed output is the input to the freeze preconditions. The sealed snapshot is the frozen evaluation's screen input (universe_and_identity.request_shapes). Every per-event request is fetched after the freeze under run_discipline.fetch.
pre_freeze_access_path.snapshot_contents: (0) The enumerated symbol list (universe_and_identity.enumeration), with its source responses. (1) Screen data for every XNYS session s from 2016-01-04 to 2020-12-31: the daily bars (adjustment raw, split and all) and official prints (auctions, with their sessions_io.official_price source labels) of sessions s-1 and s for the whole enumerated list, requested with asof = s. Also the corporate-action records from 2016-01-01 to the fetch date, and the coverage-stamp quotes of quote_coverage_stamps, requested with asof = the stamp's session. (2) The same screen data for every session from 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31, for the holdout breakpoints only (tercile_rule.holdout_breakpoints). No minute bar and no other quote is fetched before the freeze. Every part is pinned by sha256. Each page record keeps its request asof and its fetch date (the vintage) as separate fields.
pre_freeze_access_path.outputs: Per calendar year and listing exchange: symbol-sessions with a daily bar; with a raw close >= $1; with each official_price source label for the open and the close (populations.official_prints); with split, reverse-split, cash-dividend and merger records; with a suspected unadjusted split (populations.suspected_unadjusted_split). Also coverage-stamp quote counts (quote_coverage_stamps), enumerated symbols per source, and screen requests answered with no row (universe_and_identity.empty_responses).
pre_freeze_access_path.quote_coverage_stamps: Eligible-quote rates are measured only at stamps that are never v3 entry or exit stamps: 12:17 ET and 14:43 ET (12:17 and 12:43 ET on a 13:00 early close). The symbol-sessions are selected by int.from_bytes(sha256('mover-v3-coverage|' + symbol + '|' + session)[:8], 'big') % 500 == 0 among all symbol-sessions with a daily bar and a raw close >= $1, with no reference to event membership. A stamp has an eligible quote if the NBBO prevailing at the stamp is eligible (populations.fill_quote) and at most 1000 ms old, or if the first eligible quote update after the stamp arrives within 60 s. Per year, the code reports the stamps with an eligible quote, those without one, and those that are fetch-incomplete (populations.fetch_failures), and nothing else.
pre_freeze_access_path.runs: The count-only code runs once, from the committed study tree named in its output. Every run, including a failed or partial one, is appended to this registry with its revision, tree, date and output sha256. A rerun is allowed only after a failed or incomplete run, and never after its rates were read. The first complete run's output governs coverage_rule.
pre_freeze_access_path.not_allowed: No pre-freeze fetch or read of a quote at a D entry, exit or terminal-search stamp. No opening of the sealed snapshot's bars or prints by a person or by code other than the count-only code. No computation of D membership, MAX21 or any outcome.

universe_and_identity.enumeration: The symbol list for 2016-2020 and for the 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31 breakpoint sessions is the union of two sources. (a) The Alpaca asset master: GET /v2/assets with status=active and with status=inactive, class us_equity, every current exchange including OTC (today's OTC listing says nothing about 2016-2020 listing, which exclusions rule 1 decides from session data). Symbols that fail collect_daily.py DATA_SYMBOL at aa6fc79 (CUSIP-style placeholders the bars API rejects) are removed. (b) Every old and new symbol named by an Alpaca corporate-action record (GET /v1/corporate-actions, every action type, 2016-01-01 to the fetch date). This is broad-universe's supplement method (collect_daily.py and corporate_actions.py at aa6fc79), except that renamed-away tickers are kept, because per-session asof resolves them. The list is written once, sealed with the pre-freeze snapshot and pinned by sha256, and its per-source counts are count-only outputs. Survivorship limit: a name delisted in 2016-2019 that is absent from both sources cannot be discovered (broad-universe/README.md: 'names delisted in 2016-2019 without a retained action cannot be discovered from entitled sources'), so development keeps the survivorship-limited label. Holdout collection batches enumerate from the same two sources, refreshed at each batch, united with every earlier batch's list.
universe_and_identity.asof: Every request for bars, auctions (official prints) or quotes carries Alpaca's asof parameter set to a session date, never to the fetch date and never to the provider default. A screen request for session s uses asof = s. Every request for a D event decided on session t uses the event's as-known symbol with asof = t. The as-known symbol is the one under which the event appeared in the asof = t screen. Such requests cover the event's lookback (t-22 .. t-1), its minute bars, its entry, exit and terminal-search quotes and its official prints through the end of its hold or search window. A rename inside a hold or lookback is therefore resolved to the same issuer. The fetch date is kept as a separate vintage field in each page record. quotes.py fetch_one, whose PROTOCOL_ASOF is fixed at '2026-09-21', is never called.
universe_and_identity.request_shapes: The screen data are the sealed snapshot for 2016-2020 and for 2024-11 to 2025-12, and the collection batches for the holdout. The gain condition (close[t], ref(t), f(t)), the $1 floor, suspected unadjusted splits at t and exclusions 1 and 2 are evaluated on the screen data. Only the symbol-sessions that pass them are candidates, and only candidates have per-event data fetched, with asof = t. Per-event data are the minute bars for DV_reg (the last membership condition), med20, the entry bar and cum_dv; the lookback daily bars and official closes for MAX21 and exclusion 3; quotes; and hold-period prints. If a per-event official close of t or t-1 differs from the screen value, the screen value governs membership, and the difference is counted per stage.
universe_and_identity.dedup: Before membership, coverage.dedupe_identity at aa6fc79 (DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SESSIONS = 20, DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SPAN_COVERAGE = 0.98, survivor ranking by retained rename record, then price continuity, then active status, then lexicographic order) is applied to the screen table of session-s rows (each from its asof = s request). There is also a same-session guard. Two candidate D events on one session whose raw daily OHLCV (volume > 0) is identical on both s-1 and s are one event, kept under the higher-ranked symbol. Because the rows are identical, the choice cannot change any price. Pairs removed by either rule are counted per stage.
universe_and_identity.empty_responses: HTTP 200 with no row is an empty response, never silently dropped, and never fetch-incomplete (fetch-incomplete is reserved for HTTP errors and timeouts, populations.fetch_failures). Per stage, the counts reported are: enumerated symbols with no bar in the stage; screen requests with no row; and, per item, event requests with no row. Each empty event request has a fixed consequence. An empty entry-quote window is a no-entry. An empty exit or search window is a terminal exit (populations.terminal_exits), which stays in the statistic. An empty official-print response is a missing print: no event at t, or a missing H3-c leg. An empty lookback makes MAX21 undefined, so the event is unassigned.
universe_and_identity.tests: Synthetic tests with a recorded fake client cover: FB/META (a renamed-away ticker served with its successor's history under both symbols gives one event, not two); a ticker reused by a new issuer after a delisting (asof = t resolves the old issuer); a rename inside a 5-session hold (the as-known symbol with asof = t returns the whole hold); an empty exit response (a terminal exit, counted); and a request built with the fetch date as asof (refused).

populations.D_daily: Symbol-sessions t with split-consistent official-close gain close[t]/ref(t) - 1 >= 0.20 - 1e-9, where close[t] is the accepted official close of populations.official_prints and ref(t) is as populations.formulas states. They also need an official close >= $1.00 and a regular-session dollar volume DV_reg(t) >= $1,000,000. A session without an accepted official close is not an event and is counted; there is no bar fallback. The decision is at 16:15 ET on t. Entry is at the first eligible quote at or after 09:35 ET on t+1 (and at or after decision + 60 s), with an entry timeout of 300 s; otherwise there is no entry, and it is counted. The b_overnight entry is the exception (arms.b_overnight).
populations.formulas: Restated exactly, so membership does not depend on unpinned code. f(t) = (raw close / split-adjusted close on the previous XNYS session) / (the same on t), from daily bars with adjustment=raw and adjustment=split. It is set to 1 when |f - 1| <= 1e-2 or any input is missing. This is rules.split_factor's arithmetic at aa6fc79, with adjustment=split closes in place of adjustment=all closes, a deliberate departure: with adjustment=all, a cash dividend of about 1% or more would be booked as a share change. ref(t) = the accepted official close of the previous XNYS session / f(t). If that session has no accepted official close, ref(t) is undefined and t is not an event (counted). DV_reg(t) = the summed vwap x volume of the 1-minute SIP bars of session t that start at or after 09:30 ET and before the scheduled close (session_calendar); a session with no such bar has DV_reg 0. The split-consistent official-close return of session j is r(j) = C(j) x f(j) / C(j-1) - 1, where C is the accepted official close; r(j) is undefined if either close is missing. MAX21(t) = the maximum over k = 1..21 of r(t-k). These are the 21 returns of sessions t-21 .. t-1, from the 22 accepted official closes of sessions t-22 .. t-1 (the event's own session t is not in the window). If any of those closes is missing, or any session t-21 .. t-1 is a suspected unadjusted split, MAX21 is undefined and the event is unassigned (counted); there is no maximum over fewer returns. The sizing window W(t) is the 20 sessions ending at t (its close is known at the 16:15 decision). med20 = the median of DV_reg over W(t). sigma_d = the sample standard deviation (ddof = 1) of log(1 + r(j)) over the 20 sessions j of W(t). If any DV_reg or r(j) in W(t) is undefined, the trade cannot be sized and is a counted no-fill. The entry bar is the last 1-minute SIP bar of the entry session (from 04:00 ET) that is complete at the fill-decision time X, meaning it starts at or before X - 60 s. If there is none, the entry-bar cap is 0 and the trade is a counted no-fill. A synthetic test fixes each formula, including a split day, a missing previous close, a missing close inside the MAX21 window, a suspected unadjusted split inside it and an entry with no completed bar.
populations.official_prints: The accepted source labels of sessions_io.official_price at aa6fc79 are these. The listing exchange is the exchange of the largest condition-O opening print; a session with no O print has no listing exchange. Official open: opening_print_listing_exchange only. Official close: closing_print_listing_exchange or official_close_listing_exchange only. A closing_print_other_exchange, or a session with no O print, counts as no official close and is counted per year. The same rule applies to close[t], to the previous close in ref(t) and to every H3-c leg. For D, the O print of session t precedes the 16:15 ET decision by construction. The synthetic suite has one case per source label, including the rejected label and a session with a closing print but no opening print.
populations.suspected_unadjusted_split: Applied before membership. For session t, let r = raw daily close[t] / raw daily close of the previous XNYS session. Session t is a suspected unadjusted split if f(t) = 1 and |r - n| <= 0.01 x n or |r - 1/n| <= 0.01 / n for some integer n in 2..100. Such a session is not an event. Any trade whose hold spans t (from entry session to exit session) is excluded, and any event whose MAX21 window contains t is unassigned. All three are counted per stage. The rule also removes genuine moves within 1% of an integer multiple (for example +100%). That loss is preregistered and counted, not corrected.
populations.exclusions: (1) Not exchange-listed on the session: a symbol-session is eligible only if it has a listing exchange under populations.official_prints, so OTC-only trading is excluded by as-known session data. The current Alpaca asset exchange and tradable flags are never used. (2) Warrants, units and rights, by this literal rule (candidates.py at aa6fc79): exclude the symbol if (len(symbol) == 5 and re.search('[A-Z]{4}[WUR]$', symbol)) or re.search('\.(WS|U|R|W)', symbol) (Python re, unanchored search), or if it contains '/'. (3) Symbols with fewer than 21 prior XNYS sessions with a daily bar. Each exclusion is counted per stage, with a synthetic test per rule. There is no halt exclusion (halts).
populations.fetch_failures: The frozen fetch code is v3-owned and lives in the study tree. It writes page and stamp records in quotes.py's format at aa6fc79. Every request is retried up to 3 times, with waits of 1 s, 4 s and 16 s. A request that still fails with an HTTP error, a URLError or a timeout makes its stamp fetch-incomplete (a stamp_incomplete record). The run continues and does not raise. The trade that needs the stamp is excluded, not counted as a no-entry or a terminal exit, and the count is reported per item. If more than 1% of the stamps a stage requires are fetch-incomplete after the single re-fetch of run_discipline.fetch, that stage is void: every item scores p = 1 and is labelled underpowered there, with the reason stated. The rate is committed before any outcome of the stage, and a void is final. Synthetic tests cover an exhausted URLError and a timeout (each becomes stamp_incomplete, and the pool run completes), a success on the third retry, and an empty response (not fetch-incomplete).
populations.session_calendar: XNYS from exchange_calendars 4.13.2 (the version rules.py used for 2021-2026), for 2016-01-01 through the end of the last possible holdout extension. The session list, with each session's scheduled open and close, is written to the v3 data file data/session-calendar.json and pinned by sha256 at the freeze (run_discipline.data_files). A 'session' anywhere in this protocol is every scheduled XNYS trading session, early closes included. The pinned file cannot know about unscheduled future closures, such as a national day of mourning. Such a closure is removed only by a line in data/session-calendar-amendments.jsonl that cites its primary source (an NYSE notice), is committed and pushed, and is logged in the access log (purpose 'amend') before the affected session. It may concern only a date on or after the freeze session. The freeze session and N0 keep the dates computed at the freeze, and if N0 itself closes, the holdout starts at the next session. The 252-session holdout and each 63-session block count actual sessions. Synthetic tests use the 2017-07-03, 2017-11-24, 2018-11-23, 2019-12-24 and 2020-11-27 early closes and a removed session inside the holdout.
populations.session_times: Every '15:55 ET' in this protocol means the scheduled close (session_calendar) minus 5 minutes (12:55 ET on a 13:00 early close). Eligible quotes are regular-session quotes, at or after 09:30 ET and before the scheduled close. D decisions stay at 16:15 ET on early-close sessions.
populations.fill_quote: For a fill at or after time X, the quote is the NBBO prevailing at X (the latest quote update stamped at or before X) if it is eligible and X minus its timestamp is at most 1000 ms. Otherwise it is the first eligible quote update stamped after X, with the fill time equal to its timestamp. Eligible means bid > 0 and ask > bid (locked and crossed quotes excluded, as quotes.py valid_quote at aa6fc79 does) and regular session (session_times). Timeouts run from X. Synthetic tests cover a fresh prevailing quote, a stale one, a locked one and no quote inside the timeout.
populations.fill_price: Every entry and non-terminal exit fills at the mid (bid + ask) / 2 of the eligible quote that fills it, so gross returns are mid to mid. cost_model.per_side adds the per-side cost on top.

terminal_exits.search_window: An exit fills at the first eligible quote at or after its planned stamp. If none arrives before the scheduled close, the search continues session by session through the scheduled close of the 5th XNYS session after the planned exit session E (E+5). It never goes past the last session of the trade's segment (chronology.boundaries). A fill inside the window is a normal exit, flagged delayed and counted.
terminal_exits.terminal: A held position with no eligible quote in its search window is terminal. This covers a delisting, a move to OTC-only trading (outside the SIP NBBO), an SEC trading suspension, a halt that does not resume inside the window, and an exit request answered empty (universe_and_identity.empty_responses).
terminal_exits.booking: Terminal-merger: if a retained corporate-action record shows a cash or stock merger of the symbol effective on a session from the entry session through the end of the search window, the exit is booked at the last eligible bid of the hold. That is the bid of the latest eligible quote stamped after the entry fill and at or before the planned exit stamp, and merger arbitrage keeps it near the consideration. Fees are charged on that raw bid, with no further spread cost and no impact. Terminal-zero: every other terminal trade is booked at an exit value of 0, a total loss of the position, with no exit fees. This is the stated choice. Booking at the last eligible bid for all terminal trades is a sensitivity only.
terminal_exits.in_statistics: Terminal trades stay in every primary statistic, in count_unit and in the minimum samples. For each item and stage, the counts of delayed, terminal-merger and terminal-zero exits are reported. H3-c has no position: an event whose hold loses a leg this way lacks its 8 legs, is excluded from H3-c, and is counted as terminal in H3-c's report.
terminal_exits.segment_end: A trade censored at a segment end (chronology.boundaries) searches from its censoring stamp through the scheduled close of the segment's last session. With no eligible quote by then, it is terminal under the same booking and flagged censored-terminal.
terminal_exits.tests: Synthetic tests: a delisting inside a 5-session hold (terminal-zero); a delisting on a segment's last session (censored-terminal); a halt that resumes on E+3 (delayed exit); a halt that has not resumed by E+5 (terminal-zero); a cash merger effective inside the hold (terminal-merger at the last eligible bid); an empty exit response; and a check that each case is counted and kept in the statistic.

populations.corporate_actions: For every multi-session arm (b_lane, b_overnight) and each H3-c leg, deviation D7's method is restated. The exit uses the raw exit mid (the raw official print for H3-c). Shares change by the product of the split factors f(j) (populations.formulas) over the sessions after the entry session through the exit session. The rest of the adjustment=all close-to-close return over the hold is booked as cash per original share, without spread or fees. Fees use the actual exit shares and the raw exit price. H3-c legs use log((raw end print x split factor + cash) / raw start print). Mergers follow populations.terminal_exits. Synthetic tests, passed before the freeze, cross a split, an ordinary ex-dividend date and a special cash dividend of 5% (booked as cash with f = 1, never as a share change, and not flagged as a suspected unadjusted split).
populations.halts: No halt source is used, historically or prospectively, so no trade set depends on a later data purchase. As in catalyst-experiment, a halt is never inferred from missing data. An entry fills only at an eligible quote, and an entry with none inside its timeout is a counted no-entry. An exit waits for an eligible quote and becomes terminal after its search window (populations.terminal_exits). Limitation: a trade that sits through a short unobserved halt is not flagged.
populations.parameter_provenance: G = 0.20 and V = $1M are v1's loosest gain and middle volume floor. They were fixed for sample size after v1's all-negative dev/val grid was seen (a disclosed exposure) and are not tuned on any v3 window.

arms.b_lane: H1: entry as D_daily; exit at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on the 5th holding session (the entry session t+1 is holding session 1), under populations.terminal_exits
arms.a_intraday: H3-a: entry as D_daily (09:35 ET on t+1, timeout 300 s); exit at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on the entry session. Its entries are the b_lane entries of all D events, assigned or unassigned to a tercile. The overlap is intended and reported.
arms.b_overnight: H3-b: entry at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on t+1, timeout 300 s; otherwise no entry (counted). Exit at the first eligible quote at or after 09:30 ET on t+2, under populations.terminal_exits
arms.c_decomposition: H3-c, diagnostic only, not traded, gross, from official prints only: over sessions t+1 .. t+5 of every D event (no entry fill needed), the overnight legs k = 1..4 run from the official close of t+k to the official open of t+k+1, and the intraday legs k = 2..5 run from the official open to the official close of t+k. The partial first-session leg is excluded, so each event has 4 legs of each kind, and together they decompose official close(t+1) to official close(t+5). An event missing any of the 8 legs is excluded from H3-c and counted; no bar or quote substitutes, and no event is averaged over fewer legs.
arms.stops_and_sizing: No stops. Research sizing is 1x equal notional, capacity-capped (cost_model.fix_2_impact_and_capacity).

coverage_rule.scope: All five items, with one set of kept years per stage. It is decided at the freeze from the count-only outputs (exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path), before any outcome, and recorded beside multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze.
coverage_rule.no_fallback: A session or symbol without an accepted official print or an eligible quote stays a counted non-event, no-entry, terminal or excluded trade under its own rule. No bar, quote or other-exchange substitute is ever used.
coverage_rule.year_rule: A calendar year of 2016-2020 is dropped from its stage entirely (every session of that year) if its accepted official-close rate is below 90% (symbol-sessions with an accepted official close / symbol-sessions with a daily bar and raw close >= $1), or if its eligible-quote rate at the coverage stamps is below 80%. If 2016, the warm-up year, is dropped, events of early 2017 stay unassigned under tercile_rule.minimum until 60 prior events accrue. The thresholds are design choices, not measured values.
coverage_rule.item_rule: If fewer than 2 development years remain, or 2020 is dropped, no item is tested: all 5 items score p = 1 at every stage, permanently, and that is the recorded result of this protocol version.
coverage_rule.dropped_year_consequences: (a) Breakpoints: a dropped year's sessions are skipped, and a dropped year's events never enter a trailing window. (b) Segments: each edge of a dropped year is a segment boundary under chronology.boundaries, with censoring and, after it, the embargo. (c) Bootstrap: the stage's kept sessions are concatenated in date order, and the circular block bootstrap wraps over that kept list. Each has a synthetic test with a dropped middle year.
coverage_rule.limitation: The coverage stamps sample the whole $1+ universe, not movers, so mover quote coverage may be lower. Per-stage no-entry, terminal and excluded counts are reported so that this is visible.

tercile_rule.breakpoints: For an event decided on session s, the breakpoints are the 1/3 and 2/3 empirical quantiles (numpy 'linear' method) of MAX21 over all D events with a defined MAX21 whose decision session lies in the 252 kept sessions strictly before s. Every D event counts, whether it entered, had no entry or had no fill. Every input is known at the decision.
tercile_rule.holdout_breakpoints: For a holdout event, the trailing window is the 252 most recent sessions before s that lie outside the gap from 2026-01-02 to N0 - 1. That gap covers #162's reserved holdout, which v3 never reads, and every session from 2026-09-21 to N0 - 1. The window therefore draws only on (a) the sessions ending 2025-12-31 (v1/v2 validation, already exposed), whose membership comes from pre-freeze snapshot part 2, and whose per-event MAX21 lookbacks and DV_reg minute bars (asof = t) are fetched under the first granted 'count' entry, and (b) earlier holdout sessions. It reads covariates and membership only, never an outcome. A synthetic test computes the breakpoints for the first holdout session from part (a) alone.
tercile_rule.assignment: Low if MAX21 <= the 1/3 breakpoint, high if MAX21 > the 2/3 breakpoint, middle otherwise. A value equal to a breakpoint goes to the lower tercile.
tercile_rule.minimum: If fewer than 60 prior D events lie in the trailing window, the event is unassigned: it is counted and reported, and it enters neither H1 item. The 2016 warm-up year supplies the first window.

holdout.window: 252 sessions (session_calendar) starting at session N0 = the 40th session after the session of the freeze. N0 is fixed by the freeze commit alone. The freeze commit is the first commit reachable from origin/main (first-parent history) in which this file's status is frozen. The repository squash-merges pull requests, so a commit that exists only on a PR branch is never the freeze commit. Its committer timestamp, converted to America/New_York, is the freeze time. The session of the freeze is the first XNYS session whose scheduled open is at or after the freeze time. D decisions made on session N0 - 1 enter on N0 and belong to the holdout. Development and validation run by committed automation started at the freeze. The commit that adds the validation results file (with its sha256 in the run log) must be reachable from origin/main before 09:30 ET on session N0, measured by the GitHub-recorded time it became reachable (the pull request's merged_at, or the push event for a direct push). If it is not, the holdout of this protocol version is void for every item; a new protocol version is required. There is no deferral.
holdout.extension: If any carried item has fewer than its minimum holdout sample after 252 sessions (for H1-D, its smaller group), the holdout is extended in 63-session blocks, at most 2. The window is common to every carried item. A carried item still below its minimum after the second block is labelled underpowered. Each extension decision uses one 'count' read whose unit is count_unit, never an exit or outcome price.
holdout.count_unit: Integers only, keyed as follows: 'H1-D:high' and 'H1-D:low' (one integer per group, since H1-D is a difference test), 'H1-D-b_lane-low', 'H3-a', 'H3-b' and 'H3-c'. For a tradable cell or an H1-D group, the count is the trades that pass membership and every exclusion, have an entry fill quote inside the entry timeout and filled notional >= $1,000, are not fetch-incomplete, hold no suspected unadjusted split and have the tercile the key needs. Their exit is irrelevant, because terminal exits stay in the statistic (populations.terminal_exits). For H3-c, the count is the events with all 8 official legs present. Only presence and exclusion flags, decision-time inputs (MAX21, med20, the entry bar) and entry-quote presence are evaluated. No mid, spread, return or exit value is computed or emitted. The same unit applies to every minimum_sample check at every stage, and the extension rule applies to the smallest key of each carried item. A synthetic test asserts that the count output carries exactly these keys with integer values, and that the count path calls no price or return function.
holdout.why_prospective: No retrospective window free of prior mover outcomes remains: 2021-2025 is v1/v2 dev/val, 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-18 is #162's reserved holdout and is exposed at event level, 2017-2026-08-14 is broad-universe exposed at aggregate level, and 2016 is the warm-up.
holdout.accrual_exposure: The primary holdout statistic of every item uses every holdout trade; nothing is excluded for exposure. Paper exposure is recorded only for symbol-sessions in which a paper order was submitted, logged at order time (symbol, session, order id, strategy) in the collection batch's accrual log before any outcome of that trade exists. A holdout trade is paper-exposed if any session from decision t through its exit is such a symbol-session. The result without paper-exposed trades is reported only as a sensitivity. If the paper-exposed fraction of any carried item's holdout trades exceeds 5%, the holdout is labelled contaminated for that item, and the item cannot then be labelled supported (confirmatory).
holdout.holdout_read: A holdout read is exactly this: computing, from data of sessions N0 onward, any v3-defined outcome (an exit price paired with a v3 entry, a forward, net or leg return of a D event, a terminal booking) or any statistic built from one. Only such a computation inside a granted 'read' entry is permitted. A 'count' entry permits count_unit only. The following are not reads: (1) collection under holdout_gate.prospective_collection, including computing a batch's sha256; (2) live paper decisions and orders of any strategy, including the NautilusTrader paper runs and their decision streams, which are exposure and are logged in the accrual log; (3) dashboards and timers that publish metadata only (counts, liveness, freshness); (4) computing D membership without any outcome, by committed code whose output is logged in the accrual log. A synthetic test classifies one example of each case.

labels.development: disjoint from v1/v2; exposed at aggregate level through broad-universe development; screening only; survivorship-limited (names delisted in 2016-2019 without a retained corporate action cannot be discovered)
labels.validation: disjoint from v1/v2; exposed at aggregate level through broad-universe development and the S2 headline the author read; screening only, never confirmatory; the 2020 COVID regime is never dropped
labels.holdout: prospective; untouched only if the validation results commit was reachable from origin/main before 09:30 ET on N0, no holdout read preceded a committed granted access-log entry, every holdout count and read ran from the governing validation run's study tree (run_discipline.study_code), every collection batch has its committed accrual log, and no carried item's paper-exposed fraction exceeds 5%

chronology.boundaries: Segments are assigned by entry session (for H3-c, by session t+1). A trade whose planned exit falls after its segment's last session is censored: it exits at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on that last session (populations.terminal_exits.segment_end), is flagged, stays in its segment's statistics and is reported as a count. H3-b makes no entry on a segment's last session (counted). An H3-c event whose legs cross the segment end is excluded from H3-c and counted. Embargo: multi-session items (H1-D, H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-b, H3-c) give up the first 6 sessions of validation, and the first 6 kept sessions after a dropped year, as entry sessions. This keeps the censored trades of the earlier segment clear of later entries. Same-session H3-a needs no embargo. There is no embargo at N0: the holdout follows years after validation, no v3 trade is open in the sessions before N0 (those sessions are lookback inputs only), and D decisions on N0 - 1 enter on N0. A synthetic test covers the embargo after development, the embargo after a dropped year, and a 5-session trade entered on N0 that is kept.

labels.passes_stage: The item passes its stage rule. The pass has a stage-specific name: 'nominated' at development (the screen), 'screened' at validation (Holm in the 5-item family, the minimum sample and, for a tradable cell, the robustness means), and 'supported (confirmatory)' at the holdout (the same rule). Only the holdout label is a claim.
labels.not_supported_mde_excluded: The stage has at least its minimum sample, the item does not pass, and the one-sided bootstrap-percentile confidence bound (from the same B draws, numpy 'linear' quantile) at Bonferroni level a = 0.05/5 = 0.01 excludes an effect of the preregistered MDE for the realized n (minimum_detectable_effect). For the alternative 'less than 0' (H1-D), the bound is the a-quantile of the bootstrap statistics, and the MDE is excluded when that bound is greater than -MDE. For the alternative 'greater than 0' (every tradable cell, and H3-c when locked positive), the bound is the (1 - a)-quantile, and the MDE is excluded when it is less than +MDE; H3-c locked negative mirrors the 'less than 0' rule. Two-sided cases use a = 0.05/10 and require both conditions: the lower bound is greater than -MDE and the upper bound is less than +MDE. They are H3-c at development, and H3-c at later stages when multiple_testing.direction_lock found no direction. The fixed Bonferroni level is used because Holm's step-down level is not defined for items after the first retained hypothesis.
labels.underpowered: The stage is below its minimum sample, or the stage is void (populations.fetch_failures), or the item neither passes nor excludes the MDE.

outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict: H1 is not supported if H1-D is labelled not_supported_mde_excluded and H1-D-b_lane-low does not pass. H3 is not supported if H3-c is labelled not_supported_mde_excluded and neither H3-a nor H3-b passes. A verdict is computed at validation and reported as a screening verdict. For a hypothesis with a carried item, it is also computed at the holdout and reported as the confirmatory verdict. Each uses the labels of its own stage only.
outcome_reporting.validation_reporting: Every item's validation estimate, interval and label are computed and reported descriptively, whether or not development nominated it. Only nominated items receive a Holm p; the rest score p = 1 in the Holm run. The H1 high and middle b_lane cells are reported descriptively at every stage, with no p-value.
outcome_reporting.qualifiers: Contamination, lineage and deviation status are qualifiers attached to a label, never labels of their own. A holdout item that meets the pass rule while its holdout is contaminated is labelled 'screened (contaminated holdout)', never 'supported (confirmatory)'. An item labelled 'supported (confirmatory)' that is not lineage-confirmed (multiple_testing.lineage_sensitivity) carries 'lineage-unconfirmed'. A stage decided by the one permitted post-deviation rerun (run_discipline.deviations) carries 'post-deviation'.
outcome_reporting.rule: Only these three labels are used, with the qualifiers above. A result from a deviated study tree other than the permitted rerun is reported beside the governing result with no label at all. A miss is never reported as 'falsified' or as proof of no effect, and 'not supported' always states the size it excludes. A result in the direction opposite to a one-sided alternative is reported descriptively with its estimate and interval and supports no claim.

multiple_testing.family: One family of m = 5 items (item_set): H1-D, H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b, H3-c. H6 and the deferred H2, H4 and H5 are not in it.
multiple_testing.item_id_rule: item_ids is the complete list, in bytewise ASCII order. That order is used for stream spawning, for the final tie-break and for the validation results file.
multiple_testing.procedure: Holm step-down at family-wise alpha 0.05, applied separately at validation and at the holdout, over these 5 items only. An item not carried to a stage, or not tested for lack of data, scores p = 1 there. The validation results file contains all 5 validation p-values keyed by item_ids (1 for items not nominated or not tested); the evaluator refuses an incomplete file.
multiple_testing.direction_lock: H3-c is two-sided only at development, where the screen uses the two-sided p (statistics.p_value). The development results file records the sign of its development estimate. Validation and the holdout then use the one-sided test in that recorded direction, in the same Holm slot. Missing or zero estimate: if the governing development run wrote no H3-c estimate (an incomplete run, or no event with all 8 legs), or the estimate is exactly 0, no direction is recorded. H3-c then scores p = 1 at validation and at the holdout, and its label there uses the two-sided bound at a = 0.05/10 (outcome_reporting.labels). A significant result in the direction opposite to the locked one is reported descriptively and cannot pass. Synthetic tests cover a positive, a negative, a zero and a missing development estimate.
multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze: At the freeze, H1 and H3 are each recorded as either 'data in hand, tested' or 'not tested, p = 1 at every stage, permanently', by coverage_rule. Data from a new source, or a new historical range acquired after the freeze, can support only a new protocol version with its own family (v3.1+), never this family's Holm run. The prospective Alpaca SIP data collected under holdout_gate.prospective_collection are not new data in this sense.
multiple_testing.development_screen: Unadjusted p <= 0.05 with the minimum sample: one-sided in the stated direction for H1-D, H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a and H3-b, and two-sided for H3-c. Development only nominates items for validation.
multiple_testing.lineage_sensitivity: The mover question has already tried 1,012 rule-exits (v1 768, v2 244) and broad-universe-mover-v1's 60 predeclared signal variants on overlapping or other windows. Every validation and holdout p is also reported against Bonferroni 0.05 / (1012 + 60 + 5) = 4.64e-5. The archived 35-item draft computed nothing and is not counted. broad-universe's controls and descriptive lane have no pass rule and are not counted, which is a stated limitation. Each p is reported beside the normal-tail p of statistics.normal_tail_p. With B = 100,000, a bootstrap p at 4.64e-5 means at most 3 null-side draws, so the bootstrap p alone cannot resolve this level. An item is lineage-confirmed only if both its bootstrap p and its normal-tail p are at or below 4.64e-5.
multiple_testing.tie_breaks: Where items tie on a p (for example at the floor 1 / (B + 1)) in Holm ordering or in reporting, ties are broken by the normal-tail p, then by item id in bytewise ASCII order.
multiple_testing.tests_not_in_family: BH (q = 0.10) diagnostics across year, price-tier and tercile splits are reported but can never open the holdout.

minimum_sample.H3-c: the tradable_cell minima, counted as events with all 8 legs
minimum_sample.rule: A stage below its minimum reports the item as underpowered; it cannot pass that stage. Minima are counted in chronology.holdout.count_unit at every stage. For H1-D, each group (count_unit keys H1-D:high and H1-D:low) must reach the per-group minimum.

minimum_detectable_effect.formula: MDE = (z_alpha + z(0.80)) x sigma x sqrt(DEFF) x sqrt(1/n) for one cell or H3-c. For H1-D, sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2) replaces sqrt(1/n), with n1 and n2 the realized high and low group sizes. z_alpha = z(1 - 0.05/5) = 2.326 for one-sided tests, including H3-c after development. It is z(1 - 0.05/10) = 2.576 for H3-c at development and whenever H3-c has no locked direction. The MDE is computed from the planning sigma below and the realized n, and it is never re-estimated from outcomes.

sigma_by_item.rule: Every item has an entry: [planning sigma, MDE form]. 'difference' uses sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2), 'cell' uses sqrt(1/n), and 'paired' is a one-sample paired statistic with sqrt(1/n).

minimum_detectable_effect.sigma_provenance: 0.25 (the same-session close arm, H3-a) is (P95 - P5) / 3.29 from #162 v1 development aggregates for the 07:00|G0.20|V1000000 X1 exit (P5 -42.1%, P95 +39.5%), a normal approximation that understates fat tails. Those rule-exits entered at 07:00 ET in the pre-market, so the spread for 09:35 entries is not measured. The other values are assumptions with no measured source: 0.35 for the 5-session b_lane arm, 0.15 for one 15:55-to-09:30 overnight leg (H3-b), and 0.10 for the difference of two 4-leg means of log returns (H3-c). DEFF 1.5 for session clustering is also an assumption.
minimum_detectable_effect.reading: Only large effects can pass or be excluded. The literature's MAX effect (about 1% a month) is far below these MDEs, so a miss on H1-D will most likely be labelled underpowered. v3 is informative only about large mover-specific effects.

base_table.note: The v1 table, unchanged from the PR branch commit 92062e8 to main at aa6fc79. D7 records that it reproduces byte for byte under the stamp-window check. v3 refuses a table with another hash.

lookup.cell_key: time_bucket|price_tier|dv_tier, per side, from that side's fill: the time bucket of the fill timestamp, the price tier of the fill price, and the dv tier of the session's cumulative dollar volume at the fill timestamp (rules.py Bars.cum_dv: the summed vwap x volume of the session's 1-minute bars from 04:00 ET that start before the timestamp).

fix_1_monotone_dollar_volume.rule: For each time x price bucket: hs'(>= $5M) = hs(>= $5M); hs'($1-5M) = max(hs($1-5M), hs'(>= $5M)); hs'(< $1M) = max(hs(< $1M), hs'($1-5M)). A less liquid tier is never cheaper than a more liquid one.
fix_1_monotone_dollar_volume.finding: #162 review item costs-F1: cells under $1M dollar volume fell back to a time x price pool costing about half the $1-5M cell

fix_2_impact_and_capacity.notional: Filled notional = min($20,000; 1% of med20; 10% of the entry bar's dollar volume, vwap x volume), with med20 and the entry bar as populations.formulas defines them. The excess is not filled. A trade with filled notional under $1,000, or one that cannot be sized, is a no-fill and is counted.
fix_2_impact_and_capacity.impact: Impact per side (as a return) = c x sigma_d x sqrt(q), where q = filled notional / med20 and sigma_d is from populations.formulas, both known at the decision. The primary value is c = 1.0, with sensitivities at c = 0.5 and 2.0. The square-root form and the c grid are design choices bracketing the unknown.

cost_model.per_side: Cost per side = 1.25 x max(hs'(cell), h_fill) + impact, where h_fill = (ask - bid) / (ask + bid) is the realized half-spread of the fill quote as a fraction of the mid. The realized floor measures each fill's own period and quote, so the full draft's 2017-2019 re-measure of the table is not needed. The table-only cost (v1's convention) is a sensitivity. Terminal exits follow populations.terminal_exits.booking.
cost_model.fees: Fees come from data/fees-v3.json, pinned by sha256 at the freeze (run_discipline.data_files). It carries the SEC Section 31 and FINRA TAF rows in force from 2017-01-01 through the freeze, each with its primary source and quote. Rates announced after the freeze are appended only as lines of data/fees-v3-amendments.jsonl, from primary sources, committed and logged in the access log (purpose 'amend') before the first holdout count or read that uses their dates. They concern dates on or after the freeze session and never change an earlier line. #162 fees.json at aa6fc79 is not used. Alpaca commission is 0. A synthetic test looks up a 2017 and a 2019 sale and a post-freeze amended rate.
cost_model.break_even: The cost multiple at which each tradable cell's mean net return reaches 0 is reported.

statistics.estimator: The trade-level mean net return (for H3-c, the event-level mean leg difference). The median and the three robustness statistics are also reported.
statistics.bootstrap: A circular session block bootstrap, B = 100,000, over the stage's kept sessions concatenated in date order (sessions keyed by entry session; for H3-c, by t+1). Block length is 5 sessions for H3-a and 10 sessions for H1-D, H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-b and H3-c. H1-D resamples sessions jointly for both groups. The generator is numpy.random.Generator(PCG64), seeded per stage (stage_index 0 development, 1 validation, 2 holdout). Each stage uses numpy.random.SeedSequence(entropy = the first 8 bytes of sha256(frozen protocol id) read big-endian, spawn_key = (stage_index,)).spawn(5), and child i drives item_ids[i].
statistics.p_value: One-sided p = (1 + #{b : stat_b on the null side of 0}) / (B + 1). Two-sided p = min(1, 2 x the smaller one-sided p).
statistics.normal_tail_p: z = estimate / sd(the B bootstrap statistics, ddof = 1). For the alternative 'greater than 0', p_N = 1 - Phi(z); for 'less than 0', p_N = Phi(z); two-sided (H3-c at development) p_N = min(1, 2 x min(Phi(z), 1 - Phi(z))). Phi is the standard normal CDF, and p_N = 1 if the sd is 0. It is used only for lineage confirmation and tie-breaks.
statistics.robustness_required_for_a_pass: A tradable cell's validation and holdout passes also need all three of these to be > 0, each computed from that stage's trades of that cell. (1) The winsorised mean: the trade-level mean after clipping each trade net return to [q01, q99], the numpy.quantile 'linear' 0.01 and 0.99 quantiles of those returns (1% in each tail). (2) The mean without the top 5 sessions: sum trade net returns by entry session, drop the 5 entry sessions with the largest sums (a tie is broken by dropping the earlier session first), and take the trade-level mean of the remaining trades. (3) The mean of per-session means: the equal-weighted mean, over entry sessions, of each session's trade-level mean. A synthetic test fixes each on a small table.
sensitivities: validation restricted to symbol-sessions that were not a broad-universe lane decision (exposure_registry.consequence)
table-only cost, and the stress cost
every terminal-zero trade rebooked at the last eligible bid of its hold (populations.terminal_exits)

holdout_gate.opens_only_for: Items that passed validation: Holm-adjusted validation p <= 0.05 in the 5-item family, the minimum validation sample (for H1-D, in each group) and, for a tradable cell (H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b), the three robustness statistics. There is no cap: every validated item is carried. A synthetic gate test carries three validated tradable cells including H3-a, and refuses one that fails a robustness statistic.
holdout_gate.no_pass: If nothing validates, the holdout is never labelled or read, and that is the result.
holdout_gate.prospective_collection: The frozen collector (in the study tree) collects forward from the session of the freeze. Each batch holds screen data only, for the whole enumerated list (universe_and_identity.enumeration, refreshed per batch): the daily bars (raw, split and all) and official prints of sessions s-1 and s for each collected session s, with asof = s, plus corporate-action records. Batches are sealed into a private snapshot whose sha256 is committed per batch with its accrual log. No quote and no minute bar is collected, and nothing selects symbols by membership. Everything else a holdout event needs (lookbacks, minute bars, entry, exit and terminal-search quotes, hold-period prints) is fetched only under a granted 'count' or 'read' entry, by the frozen fetch code with the event's asof = t (universe_and_identity.asof), and sealed before use. Sessions from the freeze to N0 - 1 serve only as lookback inputs. No outcome is computed from any batch before a granted 'read' entry.

access_log.mode: append-only JSON lines, committed and pushed before the action each authorizes

purposes.collect: a collection batch, rows_read 0, listing that batch's accrual exposure
purposes.amend: one calendar or fee amendment line, with its primary source
purposes.count: at the end of the 252 sessions and of each extension block: count_unit per carried item, used only for the extension decision; it may fetch the entry quotes, lookbacks, minute bars and prints the count needs, under run_discipline.fetch
purposes.read: the single outcome read for carried items

access_log.rule: Any holdout read without a preceding committed granted entry of the matching purpose voids the holdout for every item. Refusals are logged too. The synthetic suite tests the 'count' path, including a test that it computes no exit price.

run_discipline.study_code: The frozen protocol records study_code = {revision: the git commit, tree: the git tree hash of blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/study/ at that commit}. The tree holds the study code, the count-only code, the fetch code, the collector, the synthetic tests and study/runtime.lock. runtime.lock pins the Python, numpy and pandas versions and exchange_calendars 4.13.2. The tree holds no data file (data_files). Every run, fetch and evaluator call names the revision, tree and runtime it ran from. Development, validation and every holdout 'count' and 'read' run from this one tree. The holdout count and read must name the same tree as the governing validation run, and the evaluator refuses any other tree (holdout_gate.evaluator_refusals). The only exception is the single rerun that run_discipline.deviations permits.
run_discipline.data_files: Data the study reads but may need to append to after the freeze live outside the study tree, in blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/data/: session-calendar.json and fees-v3.json (the base files, pinned by sha256 in the frozen protocol), and session-calendar-amendments.jsonl and fees-v3-amendments.jsonl (append-only, possibly empty at the freeze). Appending a line never changes the study tree. The run log records each amendment file's sha256 and byte length at every run, and the evaluator refuses a file whose earlier logged content is not a byte prefix of its current content.
run_discipline.run_log: blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/run-log.jsonl, append-only JSON lines. Every run of the frozen automation gets one line: each stage's fetch and re-fetch, development, validation, and each holdout 'count' and 'read', including failed and partial runs. Each line records the utc start and end, stage, purpose, study_code revision and tree, runtime lock sha256, data-file sha256s, input snapshot sha256s, status (complete, failed or partial) and the sha256 of every results file written (partial files included). For the validation results commit, it also records the GitHub-recorded time it became reachable from origin/main. Each line is committed and pushed before the next run of any stage starts.
run_discipline.once: Development is computed by one logged run and validation by one logged run. The first run of a stage that writes any outcome is that stage's governing run, whether or not it completes. The governing development run nominates, and the governing validation run's results file governs the holdout gate.
run_discipline.deviations: Any change to the study tree after the freeze is a numbered deviation in blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/deviations.json (cause, diff reference, new tree hash, affected stages), committed and pushed before any run from the new tree. A run from a deviated tree is reported beside the governing result, carries no label, and never governs a stage, the holdout gate or the extension decision. One exception: if a governing run from the frozen tree is incomplete because of an exception or an infrastructure failure, one rerun may govern, labelled 'post-deviation'. It must run under a deviation that changes no rule, and it must reproduce byte for byte every outcome the incomplete run had written. Otherwise: an incomplete development run decides development by its written outcomes alone (unwritten items score p = 1); an incomplete validation run voids the holdout of this protocol version; and an incomplete holdout read labels every carried item without a written outcome underpowered, with the reason stated.
run_discipline.fetch: Before any outcome of a stage (development, validation, and each holdout 'count' or 'read'), the frozen fetch code fetches every quote window, minute bar and official print that stage needs, under universe_and_identity.asof. It derives stamps only from decision-time inputs and quote timestamps, including the terminal-search windows. It seals the result as a sha256-pinned private snapshot, and commits that sha256 and the stage's fetch-incomplete rate in the run log. At most one re-fetch is allowed: once, of only the fetch-incomplete stamps, before any outcome of that stage, committed the same way. After it, the 1% void rule is final. No outcome is computed from unsealed data.
run_discipline.synthetic_tests: The evaluator refuses a results file from an unpinned revision or tree, a holdout count or read from a tree other than the governing validation run's, a runtime that differs from runtime.lock, an edited (not appended) amendment file, a stage with a second outcome-bearing run that no deviation covers, and an outcome computed before the stage's fetch rate is committed.

leverage_and_exits: Research runs use 1x equal notional. Paper use of any passing rule follows the README's exit and leverage policy (at most one broker-held closing order per share, the leverage-schedule-v1-20260922 ceiling, and the leverage-ladder gate rows in catalogs/us-equities/gates-20260922.json, one rung at a time). H3-b stays at 1x in any later paper use until the 2x rung and its overnight cap are clean. The edge-shrink term stays 0 until a holdout pass.

overturn: Any headline result is overturned if a rerun on the same frozen inputs, study tree and runtime.lock does not reproduce it byte for byte, if an independent quote sample puts the cost table off by more than 2x, or if the access log shows a holdout read that no committed granted entry preceded.
